newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell's Wavin sells plastic crates maker Trepak.
newsitem.headline: Shell's Wavin sells plastic crates maker Trepak.

text.p: Plastics maker Wavin BV, a 50 percent owned unit of Royal Dutch/Shell, said on Friday it had agreed to sell its subsidiary Wavin Trepak BV to the unit's management and venture capital firms ABN AMRO Participaties BV and Wadinko CV.
Wavin said Trepak is the largest manufacturer of plastic crates and transport packaging systems in the Netherlands with 150 employees and 1995 sales of 65 million guilders.
Among its clients are international groups such as Heineken, Grolsch, Ahold, Carlsberg, Krombacher, Deutsche Brunnen and Coca Cola.
Wavin said Trepak has a strong market position in the Netherlands and Germany and aims for further growth in other European countries.
Wavin decided some years ago to sell the unit as part of its policy to concentrate on its core activity of producing plastic pipes and pipe systems.

In 1994, Wavin cancelled plans to merge its Trepak unit with Germany's Berolina as it could not reach agreement with the intended German partner about property ratios and control of the planned joint venture.
